You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Micron Reclaims $1,000; Oracle’s AI Orders Face an Earnings Test; Tesla Targets Round-the-Clock Robotaxi Service (September 8, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
After Strong Payrolls, CPI Takes Over as the Test for Rate Expectations
US nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, keeping the interest-rate outlook in focus. Employment report
August CPI is scheduled for September 11 at 20:30 Beijing time, providing a key reading on inflation pressures. Official schedule
UBS’s Mark Haefele distinguishes between higher rates driven by economic growth and policy tightening prompted by inflation pressures, which have different implications for equities. Strategy commentary
Market Impact : Resilient employment supports business demand, while higher rates can weigh on valuations. For equities and crypto, the question this week is whether growth can offset inflation and interest-rate pressures.
International Commodities
China Adds Gold for a 22nd Consecutive Month
Data released on September 7 showed China’s central bank held 76.73 million troy ounces of gold at the end of August. Official reserve data
August purchases totaled 650,000 ounces, compared with 640,000 ounces in July.
This marked the central bank’s 22nd consecutive month of gold accumulation. Purchase report
Market Impact : Continued purchases support medium- and long-term demand. Near-term prices remain sensitive to US inflation data, the dollar and interest-rate expectations.
Macroeconomic Policy
Treasury Buyback Details Due as Long-End Liquidity Comes Into Focus
The US Treasury has announced larger buybacks in selected long-dated maturity buckets to support market liquidity. Treasury announcement
The official schedule calls for a preliminary list of eligible securities on September 9 and the associated operation on September 10, both in US Eastern time. Buyback schedule
Investors will watch actual purchases, participation and the response of long-term yields.
Market Impact : Any liquidity improvement will depend on execution. Changes in long-term yields also affect financing costs for capital-intensive businesses such as AI data centers.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,435.24/troy oz.
Spot Silver : Approx. $67.00/troy oz.
WTI Crude Futures : Approx. $93.15/ bbl , October 2026 contract.
Brent Crude Futures : Approx. $97.67/bbl, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approx. 98.80.
Driver Analysis : Central-bank gold purchases support demand, while US PPI and CPI will test whether inflation pressures are easing. Oil ’s contribution to inflation also matters for rate expectations. If inflation reinforces expectations of a hike, higher carrying costs could continue to weigh on precious metals.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. 78,735.29 USDT , down 1.36% over 24 hours.
ETH : Approx. 2,479.10 USDT, down 1.08% over 24 hours.
Crypto Total Market Cap : Approx. $2.76 trillion.
Driver Analysis : BTC and ETH remain below 79,000 USDT and 2,500 USDT respectively, with ETH posting the smaller 24-hour decline. US equities reopen tonight in Beijing time, and the New York Fed releases its consumer expectations survey. Watch inflation expectations and risk appetite; these round-number price levels alone do not confirm a trend reversal.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,414.25, down 0.51%.
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,718.60, down 0.38%.
Nasdaq Composite : Closed at 26,506.99, down 0.29%.
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $230.36, up 0.84%.
AAPL : $319.97, down 2.51%.
MSFT : $499.70, down 2.04%.
GOOGL : $338.46, down 1.11%.
AMZN : $258.51, down 0.15%.
META : $616.77, up 1.00%.
TSLA : $354.08, down 5.92%.
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : All three major indices declined, with the Dow falling most and the Nasdaq proving relatively resilient. Two of the Magnificent Seven advanced and five fell: Meta and Nvidia gained, while Tesla led losses and Apple and Microsoft also weakened. Rate concerns following strong employment data intersected with company-specific product, order and capacity news. Strength in selected memory stocks did not translate into a broad mega-cap technology rally. Session background
Sector Movers Observation
Semiconductors / Memory – Selected Stocks Advance
Representative stocks : Micron up 6.10%; Sandisk up 11.90%.
Drivers : Media reports of Micron’s planned HBM expansion and HBM4 production kept attention on AI-memory capacity and order execution. Capacity report
EVs / Autonomous Driving – Tesla Under Pressure
Representative stocks : Tesla down 5.92%.
Drivers : Vehicle compliance and commercial execution remain in focus after Cybercab’s launch. NHTSA has opened an inquiry, while investors continue to assess the ability to expand autonomous services. Regulatory document
Consumer Electronics – Apple Pulls Back
Representative stocks : Apple down 2.51%.
Drivers : Supply-chain reports of low initial foldable-iPhone output put the delivery ramp in focus. These reports rely on unnamed sources. Supply-chain report
III. In-Depth US Equity Analysis
[...]
Event Overview : Micron rose 6.10% to $1,016.59 in the previous session. Media reports say the company aims to lift monthly HBM capacity to about 100,000 wafers by the end of 2026 and advance HBM4 production for Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform. Capacity report
[...]
3. Tesla (TSLA) – Round-the-Clock Robotaxi Target Puts Scaling in Focus
[...]
Event Overview : Tesla fell 5.92% to $354.08 in the previous session. On September 4, its AI chief indicated that Robotaxi could move to 24-hour operation around October following the next FSD v15 integration. Current service hours are 06:00–22:00 local time; the precise scope of the expansion has not been announced. Operating plans
